source_title: Inde Navarrette on Her Awards Season Breakout, ‘Twilight’ Rewatch and More (Exclusive) - People.com
source_excerpt:
Navarrette is getting Oscar buzz for her breakout role in this year’s biggest surprise hit, ‘Obsession’
Inde Navarrette is opening up to PEOPLE in a new interview about her whirlwind year following the whopping success of Obsession
The actress is gearing up for an Oscar campaign after receiving rave reviews for her role as Nikki in the horror written and directed by Curry Barker
Navarrette says friends and family — as well as rewatching Twilight and Burlesque — have been keeping her grounded
Inde Navarrette is getting used to being recognized in public. But one fan recently found a particularly clever way to get her attention.
It happened on a Wednesday night this summer, when the 25-year-old actress was playing pool at a bar. As the darts area grew crowded, she stepped outside to join a friend. That’s when she heard a woman behind her ask, “Danielle, how are you?”
Hearing her full first name, Navarrette whipped around, trying to figure out how she knew the woman.
“I was like, ‘You sneaky little... You got me with the government [name].’ And then she was like, ‘Can I take a photo?’ I was like, ‘Honestly, girl, you kind of deserve that. This is not going to work with anybody else. You were the first and only one, but yes, you can definitely take a photo,’ ” Navarrette tells PEOPLE in a new interview.
“I think she stuck my middle name in too. I was like, ‘How do I know you? I feel like I’m getting in trouble.’ Like my mom’s here. I think it’s the funniest encounter with a fan I’ve had.”
Encounters like that are becoming increasingly common for Navarrette, whose breakout performance in Obsession has made her one of Hollywood’s most talked-about rising stars. The low-budget horror hit defied box office expectations, and now the actress is finding herself in the middle of an Oscar campaign.
Directed by 27-year-old YouTuber Curry Barker, Obsession stars Navarrette as Nikki opposite Michael Johnston , 30, as Bear. When Bear makes a wish using a cursed artifact called the One Wish Willow for his crush Nikki to love him more than anyone in the world, it comes true — and Nikki becomes, well, obsessed.
The movie was made on a budget of $750,000 and went on to break multiple box office records. After making $17.2 million in its first weekend in theaters, Obsession earned an unprecedented 39% rise in its second weekend , raking in $23.9 million. It ultimately grossed $523 million worldwide, becoming one of the highest-grossing horror movies of all time and the highest-grossing film ever made on a budget of less than $1 million.
Now, Focus Features is mounting an awards campaign for the film, with Navarrette at the center of it. According to Variety , the studio is campaigning Navarrette for Best Actress, Johnston for Best Actor and Barker for Best Director, Best Original Screenplay and Best Film Editing.
So how is Navarrette handling her sudden rise to fame? The same way she always has: leaning on family and friends.
Navarrette was born in Arizona and moved around as a child before attending high school in Redondo Beach, near Los Angeles. Growing up, she was so fiercely independent that her mom called her Inde, the first four letters of the word. After fifth grade, the name stuck.
Navarrette began acting in 2018 and went on to appear in the fourth and final season of 13 Reasons Why in 2020 and The CW’s Superman & Lois from 2021 to 2024. But nothing could have prepared her for the attention that followed Obsession ‘s release in May.
Through it all, her brothers and longtime friends have helped keep her grounded — and her routine surprisingly unchanged.
“We go to the beach. We sometimes go play pool,” Navarrette says of life after Obsession . “That’s what we did all summer was we went to the same dive bar. We played pool, we went home, we went to the beach, we did the same thing over and over again.”
She adds, “It’s really nice with friends that are saying, ‘You did a good job, but also we’re not changing our schedules.’ ”
Of course, plenty has changed in her life.
In the past month alone, Navarrette has been named one of 10 actors to watch at the Newport Beach Film Festival, mingled with Hollywood’s biggest names at the Academy Museum Gala and sat front row at Paris Fashion Week.
At all these events, she’s making friends with the people she once admired from afar — and the wisdom they’ve shared with her mirrors what she’s heard her whole life.
“A lot of what I’m hearing is take time for yourself and have fun where you can,” she says. “Be truthful to the way that you feel and don’t shy away from being yourself. And so I think those are all kind of things that I have been raised with.”
Navarrette continues, “That’s very big in my family, and so to have people also champion that inside of this industry, it’s made me feel more at home. It’s just been really cool getting that from people that I’ve always looked up to.”
Now, Navarrette is gearing up for her first time hosting Saturday Night Live on Oct. 31 (“I have so many ideas that they’re either going to give me a job or kick me out”) and for her next big role: Rogue in Marvel’s upcoming X-Men reboot.
The casting is particularly meaningful for Navarrette, who grew up watching movies every night before bed. Among her favorites were the 2000s X-Men films starring Hugh Jackman .
“I thought Rogue was the coolest, most complicated person ever,” she says. “I love this world so deeply that whenever I got the opportunity to really showcase what that character meant to me and all of that, I lost my mind. I lost my marbles.”

So much so that when she got the call that she’d booked the part, chaos ensued.
Navarrette was in a car with her boyfriend, Nick Aiello , and her makeup artist when it went down. As she tried to silently communicate the news to Aiello while still on the phone, things took a hilarious turn.
“My boyfriend was so kerfuffled with what was going on,” she recalls, that he “poured a whole Diet Coke in my bag on accident.”
“That bag is so sticky and it smells like Diet Coke, but I kind of don’t want to wash it because it’s kind of like that day,” Navarrette says, with a smile. “But yeah, it was pouring a Diet Coke in a purse kind of day.”
With awards season approaching and her career reaching new heights, Navarrette is finding comfort in familiar things — including some of the movies she loved as a kid.
“Sometimes you rekindle with yourself, you kind of do things that you loved when you were 7,” she says of what brings her joy these days. “And I recently have nonstop been watching Twilight ... So I’m going back to things that used to excite me, and that’s kind of how I’m using everything to unwind. A good shower. I took off my eyebrows. I’m trying different things to have fun and just also bring my feet back down to the ground.”
Another childhood favorite she’s been revisiting is 2010’s Burlesque , starring Christina Aguilera and Cher . Navarrette now has much in common with Aguilera’s character, who moves to Los Angeles and finds quick fame as a performer.
While getting ready for the Academy Gala, the actress put the movie on, which starts off with a cover of Etta James’ “Something’s Got a Hold on Me,” the first lyrics of which are, “Oh-oh, sometimes I get a good feeling, yeah.”
“I’m hearing Burlesque . I’m hearing everything of that movie,” Navarrette says, setting the scene. “They’re putting diamonds on my neck and I’m wearing Schiaparelli, and I’m just like, ‘Oh, sometimes I get a good feeling.’ ”
